paper_title: Realizing the efficiency-stability balance for all-polymer photovoltaic blends

knowledge_points.content: PM6-b-PY-IT is a one-pot synthesized multicomponent system consisting of PM6, PY-IT, and a block copolymer where donor (PM6) and acceptor (PY-IT) blocks are chemically bonded.
knowledge_points.evidence: In this work, we report a comparison... between the standout all-polymer blend PM6:PY-IT, and its counterpart PM6-b-PY-IT, a one-pot synthesized multicomponent system which could include: PM6, PY-IT and a co-polymer with donor and acceptor blocks chemically bonding together.

knowledge_points.content: The binary PM6:PY-IT all-polymer solar cell achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 15.24%, while the one-pot synthesized PM6-b-PY-IT system reaches a PCE of 13.63%.
knowledge_points.evidence: Consequently, the PCEs for PM6:PY-IT and PM6-b-PY-IT were 15.24% and 13.63%, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: The PM6-b-PY-IT system exhibits lower short-circuit current density (JSC of 21.51 mA cm-2) and fill factor (FF of 68.2%) compared to the binary PM6:PY-IT blend (JSC of 22.60 mA cm-2 and FF of 72.2%).
knowledge_points.evidence: The efficiency drop was due to the decreased JSC and FF... JSC (mA cm-2) 22.60... FF (%) 72.2 [for PM6:PY-IT]... JSC (mA cm-2) 21.51... FF (%) 68.2 [for PM6-b-PY-IT].

knowledge_points.content: PM6-b-PY-IT based devices experience higher levels of trap-assisted bimolecular recombination, indicated by an ideality factor (n) of 1.20 compared to 1.13 for the binary PM6:PY-IT blend.
knowledge_points.evidence: the fitted s (bimolecular recombination index) and n (ideal factor) values were 0.97 and 1.13 for PM6:PY-IT, and 0.93 and 1.20 for PM6-b-PY-IT, respectively. These results indicated that the PM6-b-PY-IT-based devices suffer higher levels of trap-assisted bimolecular recombination

knowledge_points.content: The PM6-b-PY-IT system shows lower charge carrier mobilities (hole mobility of 8.18 × 10^-4 and electron mobility of 4.67 × 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1) than the PM6:PY-IT blend, likely due to limited bi-continuity and phase purity from the block structure.
knowledge_points.evidence: the PM6-b-PY-IT-based system showed smaller μh and μe values of 8.18 × 10^-4 and 4.67 × 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1... The block copolymer containing film had a lower mobility, which might be caused by... the donor–acceptor alternatively connected structure, prompts limited bi-continuity and phase purity

knowledge_points.content: The devices in this study utilized a conventional structure with the configuration: ITO/PEDOT:PSS/active layer/PDINN/Ag.
knowledge_points.evidence: Then we fabricated devices with the configuration ITO/PEDOT:PSS/polymers/PDINN/Ag to determine the PCE differences between the two systems.

knowledge_points.content: GIWAXS analysis reveals that PM6-b-PY-IT has lower crystallinity and shorter crystalline coherence lengths (CCLs) for π-π packing compared to the PM6:PY-IT binary blend.
knowledge_points.evidence: The peak areas and crystalline coherence lengths (CCLs) of the π-π packing showed a decreasing trend from PM6:PY-IT to PM6-b-PY-IT, in both directions

knowledge_points.content: The PM6-b-PY-IT system demonstrates superior operational stability with a T80 value of 681 hours under 1 sun illumination, compared to 416 hours for the PM6:PY-IT blend.
knowledge_points.evidence: The estimated T80 value of the one pot synthesized multicomponent system was significantly higher than that of its binary counterpart (681 h > 416 h).

knowledge_points.content: PM6-b-PY-IT shows enhanced thermostability, retaining 89.8% of its initial PCE after 200 hours of baking at 80 °C, while PM6:PY-IT retains only 71.3% under the same conditions.
knowledge_points.evidence: after 200 h in a N2 glovebox baked at 80 °C, the unencapsulated devices of PM6:PY-IT retained an initial PCE of 71.3%, whereas the PCE value for PM6-b-PY-IT was 89.8%.

knowledge_points.content: The enhanced morphological stability of PM6-b-PY-IT is attributed to the chemical bonds between donor and acceptor blocks, which resist external stress-induced excessive phase segregation and surface roughness enlargement.
knowledge_points.evidence: These phenomena indicated that the existence of chemically bonded donor-acceptor blocks can resist external stress induced over phase segregation... the block copolymer will reduce such a tendency. Therefore, its morphology stability might be better than that of the traditional donor/acceptor binary system.
